A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TreeReview study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on 80 ICLR/NeurIPS papers, human evaluation, component ablations, computational costs, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds experiments on 40 papers from other scientific domains, evaluation-agreement statistics, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The question-tree decomposition, chunk selection, dynamic expansion, answer aggregation, and final review generation remain unchanged. The prompts are retained in Appendix F, formerly Appendix E. The compact-tree experiment tests a configuration of the existing method.

E1.justification: Section 4.5 adds evaluation on 40 Nature Communications papers: 13 biology, 14 climate science, and 13 quantum science papers. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained AI/ML benchmark, using both existing review-generation tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new domain evaluation reuses existing baselines: DGE and SORT for full reviews, and DPW and SORT for actionable comments.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a controlled comparison of initial tree widths 5/4/3 versus 4/3/2, keeping the expansion limit at two. Appendix E.3 introduces paper-type grouping and analysis of the lowest-performing 20%. The original benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially broadens analysis beyond the retained component ablations and case study. It adds cross-domain generalization, LLM–human agreement analysis, a single-paper tree-configuration sensitivity study, qualitative failure analysis, and performance analysis by paper type.

E5.justification: Section 4.4 newly reports Spearman correlation between LLM scores and human win rates, approximately 0.90 with p < 0.05. Appendix E.3 also reports nonsignificant paper-type tests without specifying them. Existing scoring-run counts, ICC, and human agreement reporting are retained.

E6.justification: New Tables 3–4 report substantial additional results on the cross-domain dataset, including TreeReview overall quality of 8.31, comment precision of 34.62%, and Jaccard of 17.68%. New agreement, sensitivity, and failure findings are also reported. Original benchmark results remain unchanged; the new scores concern different data.

T1.justification: The method equations and mathematical definitions in Appendices A and C are retained. V2 introduces no new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about TreeReview, its benchmark, review quality, and token efficiency. New generalization evidence does not alter those core statements.

C2.justification: V1 identifies cross-domain generalization as unexplored; v2 interprets its new experiments as supporting broader scientific applicability. V2 also adds tree-robustness explanations, paper-type hypotheses, specific visual and cross-section consistency failure modes, and limitations concerning backend knowledge and hallucination.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 supplies explicit hyperparameters for the new compact-tree comparison, including widths 4/3/2 and an expansion limit of two. Existing implementation details, hardware, prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds historical context and six references covering reviewer assignment, plagiarism detection, rating recommendation, and earlier review-generation models. The existing LLM and task-decomposition positioning is retained. The survey's preprint-to-journal update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: V2 renames Section 2.1, expands task motivation, inserts a generalization section and Further Analysis appendix, and relabels the retained prompts appendix. Author information and acknowledgements also change, while most existing prose and organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds two cross-domain results tables and adjusts float placement and several table-caption positions. Existing figures retain identical image content; other tables are retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 partially addresses v1's explicitly untested cross-domain applicability, adds an LLM–human agreement check, and documents concrete failure conditions. These strengthen empirical support and critical discussion. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new dataset and paper-type tests, while the single-paper tree study provides limited support for its broad robustness interpretation.
